### Script for Analysis of CyCIF CRC dataset for "Are low-variance Principal Components of single-cell omics data biologically meaningful, or just noise?"
### Data source. 
# https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674(22)01571-9
#### cell tables:  (Sardana_CRC_46.csv Sardana_CRC_47.csv) were generated with the scripts in the t-CyCIF ImageJ/MATLAB pipeline(https://github.com/sorgerlab/cycif) repo
### Quality control; PCA on 24 tumor markers (section 47); mean marker intensity of the 40 nearest non-epithelial cells (section 46); CCA; permutation test; Multivariate regression; figure panels.
### Inputs: mmc3.xlsx  Sardana_CRC_46.csv Sardana_CRC_47.csv
### Outputs: panels for figure 4.


### Library 
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(RANN)   
library(zoo)
library(readxl)

###plotting
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)
library(pheatmap)
library(svglite)
library(reshape2)
library(grid)
```



### Functions
```{r}
### Summary function   
print_cv_summary <- function(xload, yload, cca_cors, n_pc, label) {
  # xload: correlations between tumor PC scores and tumor-side CV scores, U.
  # yload: correlations between immune-neighborhood markers and neighborhood-side CV scores, V.
  # cca_cors: canonical correlation for each CV, cor(U, V).
  # n_pc: number of tumor PCs.
  # label: name printed above this CCA result.
  
  
  cat(paste0("\n=== ", label, " ===\n\n")) 
  n_cv <- length(cca_cors)   
 
   for (cv in 1:n_cv) { 
    loads <- xload[, cv]  # Tumor PC loading for this tumor-side CV score.
    
    contrib <- loads^2 / sum(loads^2) ### Square PC loadings and normalize them to sum to 1 to obtain the relative squared-loading composition of each CV.
    names(contrib) <- paste0("PC", 1:n_pc)
    
    top5 <- sort(contrib, decreasing = TRUE)[1:5]  ### Top 5 pcs by normalized squared loading.
    #PCs 9–24 are the low-variance group (each ≤ 2.4% of variance)
    early <- round(sum(contrib[1:8]) * 100, 1)  ### Percentage of normalized squared PC-loading magnitude from PCs 1-8.
    late <- round(sum(contrib[9:n_pc]) * 100, 1) ### Percentage of normalized squared PC-loading magnitude from PCs 9-n_pc.
    
    imm_loads <- yload[, cv] ### Correlation of each neighborhood marker with the neighborhood-side CV score
    top_idx <- order(abs(imm_loads), decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]
    imm_top3 <- imm_loads[top_idx]  ### Top immune markers.
    ### Print out results. 
    cat(sprintf("CV%d (r=%.3f) | Early: %.1f%% Late: %.1f%% | Top PCs: %s | Top immune: %s\n",
                cv, cca_cors[cv], early, late,
                paste(names(top5), sprintf("%.1f%%", top5*100), sep="=", collapse=", "),
                paste(names(imm_top3), sprintf("%.2f", imm_top3), sep="=", collapse=", ")))
  }
}


### Run CCA and return loading.
run_cca <- function(pca_obj, neighborhood_df, pc_cols_use) { 
  reg <- data.frame(pca_obj$x[, 1:length(pc_cols_use)]) ### Extract selected tumor PC scores.
  colnames(reg) <- pc_cols_use 
  reg[pc_cols_use] <- scale(reg[pc_cols_use]) ###scale the pc scores such that each PC is standardized to unit variance before CCA so high-variance  PCs do not dominate solely because of their high variance
  
  Y <- as.matrix(neighborhood_df[, -1]) #### drop tumor cell id from means 
  X <- as.matrix(reg[, pc_cols_use])   
  
  cca_out <- cancor(X, Y) ###CCA between tumor cells PC scores and immune means 
  
  X_c <- scale(X, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)  
  Y_c <- scale(Y, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE) 
  U <- X_c %*% cca_out$xcoef ### Calculate tumor-side canonical scores (U). 
  V <- Y_c %*% cca_out$ycoef ### Calculate neighborhood-side canonical scores (V). 

  ### Calculate canonical loading as correlations between input variables and canonical scores.
  xload <- cor(X, U) 
  yload <- cor(Y, V)
  ### Return CCA results, loading, and canonical scores. 
  list(cca = cca_out, xload = xload, yload = yload, U = U, V = V)
}


###significance test, sub sample x side and shuffle y side 

sig_test_shuffle <- function(
  seed, ### Random seed.
  n_perm, ### Number of permutations.
  n_sub,  ### Number of cells in the sub sample.
  pca_res, ### Tumor PCA object.
  nbr_data, ## Section 46 non-epithelial cells: marker intensities and Xt, Yt coordinates
  tumor_coords, #### Tumor-cell spatial coordinates.
  immune_cols_CCA,  ### the cols to take the means of 
  nbr_means         ### precalced nbr means to do baseline CCA 
  
) {

  ### set seed for reproducibility  
  set.seed(seed)

  ### z score the x side scores 
  X_scores <- as.matrix(scale(pca_res$x))
  
  tumor_coords <- tumor_coords[, c("Xt", "Yt")]
  
  ### get the non mean section 46 intensity data 
  S_46_markers <- nbr_data[,immune_cols_CCA]
  ### get the non mean section coords 46 data 
  S_46_coorads <- nbr_data[,c("Xt","Yt")]
  
  ### join into one DF 
  full_46 <- bind_cols(S_46_markers,S_46_coorads)
  
  ### check they all match up 
  stopifnot(
    nrow(X_scores) == nrow(tumor_coords),
    nrow(X_scores) == nrow(nbr_means),
    n_sub <= nrow(X_scores),
    all(immune_cols_CCA %in% colnames(nbr_data)),
    all(immune_cols_CCA %in% colnames(nbr_means))
  )
  
  #### baseline sampled CCA to compare the null too 
  ### Sub sample cells.
  sub_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(X_scores)), n_sub)
  
  ### get the  NBR means values
  Y_perm <- as.matrix(nbr_means[, immune_cols_CCA])
  
  ### get the matching PC scores (scaled) from the subset 
  X_sub <- X_scores[sub_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  
  ### get the matching tumor coordinates from the subset
  tumor_coords_sub <- tumor_coords[sub_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  ### get the NBR means the correspond to the sampled X cells 
  Y_sub <- Y_perm[sub_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  
  
  
  ### Observed CCA on the sub sample.
  obs_sub <- cancor(X_sub, Y_sub)$cor
   
  ##storage for the null cors 
  null_cors_block <- matrix(
      NA_real_,
      nrow = n_perm,
      ncol = length(obs_sub)
    )
  
  
  ### get the marker values for section 46 
  full_46_markers_only <- full_46 %>% select(-Xt,-Yt)
  ### the X and Y values for the y side (section 46)
  X_Y_to_shuffle <- cbind(full_46$Xt,full_46$Yt)
  
  
  ### start the perm loop
  for (i in seq_len(n_perm)) {
    ### shuffle the Y side coords, so each cell now has a diff X and Y 
    X_Y_shuffled <- X_Y_to_shuffle[sample(1:nrow(X_Y_to_shuffle)),]
    
    full_46_markers_only_shuffled_coords <- full_46_markers_only
    
    full_46_markers_only_shuffled_coords$Xt_shuff <- X_Y_shuffled[,1]
    full_46_markers_only_shuffled_coords$Yt_shuff <- X_Y_shuffled[,2]
    
    ### Identify nearest neighbors in registered spatial coordinates. Using all Y cells but sampled X cells, so now each x cell has 40 nn Neighbors that have been shuffled 
    nn_nonepi_shuffled <- nn2(
      data  = full_46_markers_only_shuffled_coords[, c("Xt_shuff", "Yt_shuff")], #### Reference cells: non-epithelial cells from section 46
      query = tumor_coords_sub[, c("Xt", "Yt")], ### Query cells: tumor cells from section 47.
      k = 40 ### Number of nearest neighbors.
    )
    
    ###find means 
    ##so  each of the sampled X cells will have the mean values of markers from shuffled cells 
    nbr_means_shuffled <- data.frame(tumor_cell = 1:nrow(X_sub))
    
    for (col in immune_cols_CCA) {
      nbr_means_shuffled[[col]] <- apply(nn_nonepi_shuffled$nn.idx, 1, function(idx) {
        mean(full_46_markers_only_shuffled_coords[[col]][idx])
      })
    }
    ### run CCA comparing the sampled X cells PC values to the shuffled means 
    null_cors_block[i,] <- cancor(X_sub, as.matrix(nbr_means_shuffled[, immune_cols_CCA]))$cor
    
    
    ###print out progress every 100 permutations.
      if (i %% 100 == 0) {
        cat("Permutation", i, "/", n_perm, "\n")
        }
  
  ### end of perm loop 
  }
    # Summary table
    perm_sig <- data.frame(
      CV = seq_along(obs_sub), ### CV number 
  
      r_sub = round(obs_sub, 4), ### Observed canonical correlations in the subsample 
  
      null_mean = round(colMeans(null_cors_block), 4),  ### Mean null canonical correlation for each CV.
  
      null_95 = round(apply(null_cors_block, 2, quantile, 0.95), 4),####95th percentile of the null distribution for each CV
  
      ratio = round(obs_sub / colMeans(null_cors_block), 1), ### Ratio of observed to mean null canonical correlation.
      p_value = sapply(seq_along(obs_sub), function(j) {   # p val 
        ( sum(null_cors_block[, j] >= obs_sub[j])) / (n_perm) })
    
      )
    ### BH correction 
  perm_sig$p_adj <- p.adjust(perm_sig$p_value, method = "BH")
    
    print(perm_sig)
  
    cat("\nSignificant CVs (p < 0.05):", sum(perm_sig$p_value < 0.05),"\n" )
  
    cat("Significant CVs (BH-adjusted p < 0.05):", sum(perm_sig$p_adj < 0.05), "\n")
  
    # Return everything required for summaries and plots
    list(
      results = perm_sig,
      null_cors = null_cors_block,
      observed = obs_sub,
      sample_indices = sub_idx,
      coords = tumor_coords_sub
    )
}

### plotting functions 

# SVG device: map generic sans font to Arial
### Save Plot as SVG 
arial_svg <- function(filename, width, height, ...) {
  svglite::svglite(
    file = filename,
    width = width,   ### Width of output
    height = height, ### height of output

### Order and group marker weights per CV

order_markers_by_cv <- function(coef_mat) {
  best_cv <- apply(abs(coef_mat), 1, which.max) ### In which CV column does a marker have its largest absolute coefficient.
  best_val <- apply(abs(coef_mat), 1, max)     ### For each marker, grab that largest absolute coefficient for sorting.

  ord <- order(best_cv, -best_val) ### Sorts first by assigned CV (highest abs weight), then within assigned CV.

  gaps <- cumsum(table(best_cv[ord])) ### Cumulative row positions where each CV group ends, tells pheatmap where to draw gaps.
  gaps <- gaps[-length(gaps)]       

  annot <- data.frame(   
    CV = paste0("CV", best_cv[ord]),
    row.names = rownames(coef_mat)[ord])

  list(
    order = ord,
    gaps = gaps,
    annotation = annot)
}



```




### Setup. 
```{r}

panel_path <- file.path("Data/mmc3.xlsx")    #### Marker-panel reference file.

csv_dir    <- file.path("Data/Raw_CRC_CSV") ### Raw CRC CSV directory.

out_dir_plots    <- file.path("Data/Plots") ### Output directory for figure panels.

dir.create(out_dir_plots, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) ### Create the output folder for figure panels.

```

## Part 1: Quality control.

## Step 1: Build the channel → marker rename lookup.
```{r}

### Load the marker-panel reference table.
raw_ref <- read_excel(panel_path, sheet = "CRC1 slices 45-47", col_names = FALSE) 

colnames(raw_ref) <- c("cycle_raw", "channel", "s45", "s46", "s47")

raw_ref <- raw_ref[-1, ]

raw_ref$cycle_raw <- zoo::na.locf(raw_ref$cycle_raw, na.rm = FALSE)
### Standardize fluorescence channel/cycle identifiers and map them to section-specific protein-marker names.
ref <- raw_ref %>%
  mutate(
    cycle   = as.integer(str_extract(cycle_raw, "\\d+")),
    channel = recode(channel, A488 = "FITC", A555 = "Cy3", A647 = "Cy5"),
    csv_col = paste0(channel, "_", cycle),
    across(c(s45, s46, s47), ~ sub("\\s*\\(.*", "", .x))
  ) %>%
  select(cycle, channel, csv_col, s45, s46, s47)
```





## Step 2: Read raw CSVs and rename columns. 
```{r}
### Read one CRC section and replace fluorescence channel/cycle column names with the corresponding protein-marker names from the panel lookup.
rename_section <- function(sec) {
  dat <- read.csv(file.path(csv_dir, paste0("Sardana_CRC_", sec, ".csv")))
  ### Select the marker identities corresponding to the requested section.
  lookup <- ref %>% select(csv_col, marker = all_of(paste0("s", sec)))
  
  ### Match raw channel/cycle columns (e.g., Cy3_5) to marker names.
  idx <- match(colnames(dat), lookup$csv_col)
  new_names <- ifelse(is.na(idx), colnames(dat), lookup$marker[idx])
  ### if same marker was measured in more than one imaging cycle append the cycle number so the resulting name is unique
  dupes <- unique(new_names[duplicated(new_names)])
  if (length(dupes) > 0) {
    for (i in seq_along(new_names)) {
      if (new_names[i] %in% dupes & !is.na(idx[i])) {
        cycle_num <- str_extract(lookup$csv_col[idx[i]], "\\d+$")
        new_names[i] <- paste0(new_names[i], "_c", cycle_num)
      }
    }
  }
  ### Convert marker names to valid R column names.
  colnames(dat) <- make.names(new_names)   
  return(dat)
}
### Import and rename the two CRC sections used in downstream analysis.
crc_46 <- rename_section("46")
crc_47 <- rename_section("47")
### Report dataset dimensions as a basic import check.
cat("Section 46:", nrow(crc_46), "cells,", ncol(crc_46), "columns\n")
cat("Section 47:", nrow(crc_47), "cells,", ncol(crc_47), "columns\n")

### Correct marker annotation: antibody corresponds to FOXO1 rather than FOXA1. 
colnames(crc_47)[colnames(crc_47) == "FOXA1"] <- "FOXO1"
```



## Step 3: Drop bad channels.

### Channels dropped for quality reasons (staining artefacts, poor signal quality, or late-cycle tissue loss).

```{r}
### Marker channels excluded for quality reasons.
bad_46 <- c("PAX5", "POLR2A", "NFATc1", "PAX8", "pBTK", "VEGFR2","CD11a","CD16","CD1a","CD57") 
bad_47 <- c("EZH2", "pCDK", "E2F1", "FOXA2", "CD20","SMA_c9","SMA_c10","H3","NCR1") 

crc_46 <- crc_46[, !colnames(crc_46) %in% bad_46]
crc_47 <- crc_47[, !colnames(crc_47) %in% bad_47]

cat("Section 46: dropped", length(bad_46), "bad channels →", ncol(crc_46), "columns\n")
cat("Section 47: dropped", length(bad_47), "bad channels →", ncol(crc_47), "columns\n")
```




### Step 4: Filter cells with zero intensity in any marker channel.

### Cells with zero intensity in any retained marker channel were excluded as potential technical failures, including tissue loss.

```{r}
### Select marker-intensity columns after bad-channel removal.
### Secondary-antibody channels are excluded from the zero-intensity filter.

### Identify marker columns used for zero-intensity filtering.
get_marker_cols <- function(dat, start, end) {
  cols <- colnames(dat)[start:end]
  cols[!grepl("anti", cols)]
}

marker_46 <- get_marker_cols(crc_46, 15, 46)
marker_47 <- get_marker_cols(crc_47, 15, 47)

### Identify cells with zero intensity in any retained marker.
has_zero_46 <- apply(crc_46[marker_46], 1, function(x) any(x == 0))
has_zero_47 <- apply(crc_47[marker_47], 1, function(x) any(x == 0))

### Remove cells containing zero-intensity marker measurements.
crc_46 <- crc_46[!has_zero_46, ]
crc_47 <- crc_47[!has_zero_47, ]

### Report the number of excluded cells.
cat("Section 46: removed", sum(has_zero_46), "cells with zeros →", nrow(crc_46), "cells\n")
cat("Section 47: removed", sum(has_zero_47), "cells with zeros →", nrow(crc_47), "cells\n")
```



### Step 5: Filter cells with unstable Hoechst signal across cycles. 
### Cells with high CV across the 14 Hoechst measurements may have experienced tissue loss or photobleaching in later cycles. Cells with unusually low CV may indicate segmentation artifacts. 
### We exclude cells beyond ±3 SD of the mean CV.

```{r}
### Hoechst intensity columns measured across imaging cycles.
hoechst_cols <- paste0("Hoechst_", 1:14)

### Section 46   

### Calculate the coefficient of variation (CV) of Hoechst intensity  across the 14 measurements for each cell.
cv_46 <- apply(crc_46[hoechst_cols], 1, function(x) sd(x) / mean(x))


### Define outlier thresholds as 3 SD above or below the mean Hoechst CV.
upper_46 <- mean(cv_46) + 3 * sd(cv_46)
lower_46 <- mean(cv_46) - 3 * sd(cv_46)


### Report the number of cells outside the CV thresholds.
cat("S46 — above upper:", sum(cv_46 > upper_46), "\n")
cat("S46 — below lower:", sum(cv_46 < lower_46), "\n")
cat("S46 — total flagged:", sum(cv_46 > upper_46 | cv_46 < lower_46), "\n")

### Repeat the Hoechst CV calculation and outlier detection for section 47.
cv_47 <- apply(crc_47[hoechst_cols], 1, function(x) sd(x) / mean(x))
upper_47 <- mean(cv_47) + 3 * sd(cv_47)
lower_47 <- mean(cv_47) - 3 * sd(cv_47)

### Report the number of cells outside the CV thresholds.

cat("S47 — above upper:", sum(cv_47 > upper_47), "\n")
cat("S47 — below lower:", sum(cv_47 < lower_47), "\n")
cat("S47 — total flagged:", sum(cv_47 > upper_47 | cv_47 < lower_47), "\n")

### Flag cells whose Hoechst CV lies outside the section-specific ±3 SD range.
cv_flag_46 <- cv_46 > upper_46 | cv_46 < lower_46
cv_flag_47 <- cv_47 > upper_47 | cv_47 < lower_47
```



### Step 6: Apply Hoechst CV filter to filter cells beyond ±3 SD of the mean CV.
```{r}
### Remove cells flagged by the Hoechst CV filter.
CV_drop_46 <- cv_flag_46
CV_drop_47 <- cv_flag_47 
crc_46 <- crc_46[!CV_drop_46, ]
crc_47 <- crc_47[!CV_drop_47, ]

cat("Section 46: removed", sum(CV_drop_46), "cells (CV) →", nrow(crc_46), "cells\n")
cat("Section 47: removed", sum(CV_drop_47), "cells (CV) →", nrow(crc_47), "cells\n")
```




### Step 7: Log-transform marker intensities to reduce skew in marker-intensity distributions.

### log1p (log(1+x)) is used to accommodate small non-negative intensity values.
```{r}
### Recalculate marker cols after filtering
marker_46 <- get_marker_cols(crc_46, 15, 46)
marker_47 <- get_marker_cols(crc_47, 15, 47)

crc_46[marker_46] <- log1p(crc_46[marker_46])
crc_47[marker_47] <- log1p(crc_47[marker_47])

cat("Log-transformed", length(marker_46), "markers on section 46\n")
cat("Log-transformed", length(marker_47), "markers on section 47\n")
```




### Part 2: CCA analysis.

### Step 1: ROI and region exclusion.

### ROI-1 excluded for being non-cancerous normal colon mucosa.

```{r}
# Remove ROI 1 (normal mucosa).
filter_region <- function(dat) {
  dat %>%
    filter(ROI != 1) 
}


###drop cells tagged with roi 1.
crc_46_filtered <- filter_region(crc_46)
crc_47_filtered <- filter_region(crc_47)

cat("S46:", nrow(crc_46), "→", nrow(crc_46_filtered), "after region exclusion\n")
cat("S47:", nrow(crc_47), "→", nrow(crc_47_filtered), "after region exclusion\n")
```


### Step 2: Label cells 

### Different epithelial markers were used because the two sections contained different staining panels.

###Section 46: Epithelial gating  

### PanKeratin threshold (5.2) was selected from the bimodal distribution of log1p-transformed PanKeratin intensity to classify epithelial cells.
```{r}
crc_46_gated <- crc_46_filtered %>%
  mutate(is_epi = panKeratin > 5.2 ) ### Classify PanKeratin-high cells as epithelial.
```






### Section 47: Tumor gating

### E-cadherin threshold (6.8) was selected from the bimodal distribution of log1p-transformed E-cadherin intensity to identify tumor epithelial cells.
```{r}
ecad_threshold <- 6.8


tumor_47 <- crc_47_filtered %>% filter(E.cadherin > ecad_threshold) ### Retain E-cadherin-high cells as tumor epithelial cells.
```




### Step 3: PCA on tumor cells.

#### PCA was used on log1p-transformed tumor-marker intensities to summarize correlated tumor-marker intensities into orthogonal components ordered by the amount of variation captured across tumor cells.


### Marker intensities were mean-centered but not variance-scaled before PCA, so differences in variance among markers were retained.

```{r}
## PCA on tumor cells with relevant markers 
pca_markers <- c("RPA32", "SDHB", "NP.Catenin", "EGFR", "Bax", "MucinAC",
                  "cJUN", "LaminB1", "BRAFV600E", "Notch1", "pTBK1", "pH3",
                  "TriMeH3", "FOXO1", "E.cadherin", "KAP1", "S100A4",
                  "COXIV", "cCasp3", "Survivin", "p53", "ERBB2", "NGFR", "mTOR")
### Verify that all selected markers are present.
stopifnot(all(pca_markers %in% colnames(tumor_47)))


pca_result_47 <- prcomp(tumor_47[pca_markers], center = TRUE, scale. = F) ### Mean-center markers without variance scaling.

### Calculate the fraction of variance explained by each PC. 
var_explained<- pca_result_47$sdev^2 / sum(pca_result_47$sdev^2)
round(var_explained * 100, 1)
```



### Step 4: Nearest-neighbour mapping.

### Sections 46 and 47 have previously been spatially registered, so Xt and Yt coordinates are expressed in the same coordinate system.

### For each tumor cell in section 47, the 40 nearest non-epithelial cells in registered section 46 were identified using Xt and Yt coordinates.

### k=40 nearest non-epithelial neighbors selected as a balance between spatial resolution and stable CCA estimates.

```{r}
### Filter out cells labeled as epithelial
crc_46_nonepi <- crc_46_gated %>% filter(!is_epi)

### Identify nearest neighbors in registered spatial coordinates.
nn_nonepi <- nn2(
  data  = crc_46_nonepi[, c("Xt", "Yt")], #### Reference cells: non-epithelial cells from section 46
  query = tumor_47[, c("Xt", "Yt")], ### Query cells: tumor cells from section 47.
  k = 40 ### Number of nearest neighbors.
)
```



### Step 5: Calculate the mean log-transformed marker intensities of the NN.

### For each tumor cell, the mean log1p-transformed marker intensity was calculated across its 40 nearest non-epithelial cells to summarize the local non-epithelial microenvironment.

```{r}
### Neighborhood markers analyzed in section 46. 
immune_cols <- c("CD3", "CD4_c3", "CD8a", "CD45", "CD68", "CD163",
                 "CD11c", "CD11b", "IBA1", "GranB", "CD14_c3",
                 "PD.1", "HLA.A", "CD31", "PD.L1_c5")


nbr_mean_nonepi <- data.frame(tumor_cell = 1:nrow(tumor_47)) ### Initialize one neighborhood-summary row per tumor cell.

### Calculate the mean log1p-transformed intensity of each marker across the 40 nearest non-epithelial cells.
for (col in immune_cols) { 
  nbr_mean_nonepi[[col]] <- apply(nn_nonepi$nn.idx, 1, function(idx) { 
    mean(crc_46_nonepi[[col]][idx])
  })
}

```

### Step 6: Run CCA

### CCA was used to identify paired linear combinations of tumor PC scores and neighborhood marker intensities that show maximal correlation across cells

### All 24 tumor PCs were used on the tumor side, and mean intensities of the selected non-epithelial neighborhood markers were used on the neighborhood side.

### PC scores were z-scored before CCA.

```{r}
pc_cols_24 <- paste0("PC", 1:24)

###run CCA
res_ne_47    <- run_cca(pca_result_47, nbr_mean_nonepi, pc_cols_24)

####print summary 
print_cv_summary(res_ne_47$xload,  res_ne_47$yload,  res_ne_47$cca$cor,  24, "MEAN INTENSITY — NON-EPI")

```

### step 7: Significance tests 

### permutations were used to generate a null distribution

### For a 10,000-cell subsample of tumor cells, the coordinates of the section 46 non-epithelial cells are shuffled and the neighborhood means recomputed, 500 times
```{r}
sig_test_shuffle(seed = 42,  ### seed for reproducibility 
                 n_perm = 500, ### number of permutations 
                 n_sub = 10000,   ### number of cells to sub sample 
                 pca_res = pca_result_47,   ### pca results 
                 nbr_data =crc_46_nonepi,   ### NBR marker values and coords
                 tumor_coords = tumor_47[, c("Xt", "Yt")],  ### tumor (section 47) coords 
                 immune_cols_CCA = immune_cols,            ### string vector of immune cols for CCA 
                 nbr_means =  nbr_mean_nonepi )            ### base line NN means for baseline sampled CCA 


```



### Step 8: Multivariate regression.

### Tumor and neighborhood-side canonical variate scores were regressed on z-scored marker intensities to express each canonical variate in standardized marker space.

### Each coefficient is that marker's weight in the CV score with the other markers held fixed

```{r}
CV_U_for_lm <- res_ne_47$U ### Extract tumor-side canonical scores.

tumor_47_for_lm_scaled <- scale(tumor_47[pca_markers]) ### Z-score tumor-marker intensities.


CV_U_for_lm_fit <- lm(CV_U_for_lm ~ tumor_47_for_lm_scaled) ### Fit multivariate regression models for tumor-side CV scores.

coefs_U <- CV_U_for_lm_fit$coefficients[-1, 1:6]  # drop intercept, keep CV1-6 weights 

### rename 
### The first six CVs are shown in Figure 4
colnames(coefs_U) <- paste0("CV", 1:6) 
rownames(coefs_U) <- pca_markers



### Repeat for neighborhood-side canonical scores.
CV_V_for_lm <- res_ne_47$V ##get NN side score 

imunne_for_lm_scaled <- scale(nbr_mean_nonepi[,-1]) ### Z-score neighborhood marker means. 


CV_V_for_lm_fit <- lm(CV_V_for_lm ~ imunne_for_lm_scaled) ### Fit multivariate regression models for neighborhood-side CV scores.

coefs_V <- CV_V_for_lm_fit$coefficients[-1, 1:6]  # drop intercept, keep CV1-6
###rename 
colnames(coefs_V) <- paste0("CV", 1:6)
rownames(coefs_V) <- immune_cols

```





### Part 3: Figure panels
### Figure 4 A
```{r}
# Plot 1: PC composition.

### Extract tumor PC loading for the first 15 CVs.
pc_loads <- res_ne_47$xload[, 1:15]  

## Convert squared PC loading to percentage composition within each CV.
contrib <- apply(pc_loads^2, 2, function(x) x / sum(x)) * 100 
colnames(contrib) <- paste0("CV", 1:15)
rownames(contrib) <- paste0("PC", 1:24)

###reshape data for plotting.
pc_pct_long <- reshape2::melt(contrib)
colnames(pc_pct_long) <- c("PC", "CV", "pct")
pc_pct_long$PC <- factor(pc_pct_long$PC, levels = rev(paste0("PC", 1:24)))
pc_pct_long$CV <- factor(pc_pct_long$CV, levels = paste0("CV", 1:15))
max_pct <- max(c(contrib, var_explained * 100))
pc_pct_long_plot <- pc_pct_long %>% 
  filter(CV %in% paste0("CV",1:6))


###make plot. 
p_pc_with_legend <- ggplot(pc_pct_long_plot,aes(x = CV, y = PC, fill = pct)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white",linewidth = 0.3,width = 1) +
  geom_hline( yintercept = 16.5,linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F0F0F0",high = "#B2182B",name = "%",limits = c(0, max_pct)) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_colorbar(
      title = "%",
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      barheight = grid::unit(1.5, "cm"),
      barwidth = grid::unit(0.3, "cm"))) +
  labs(title = "PC Composition",x = NULL,y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8, base_family = "sans") +
  theme( 
    plot.title = element_text(family = "sans", size = 8, hjust = 0.5,face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(family = "sans", size = 8, angle = 0),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(family = "sans", size = 8, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 3)),
    legend.text = element_text( family = "sans", size = 8),
    text = element_text(family = "sans", size = 8)
    )


### Extract the shared percentage color legend.
pct_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(p_pc_with_legend +
    theme(legend.position = "right"))

# Main PC plot without legend.
p_pc <- p_pc_with_legend +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Preview

print(p_pc)

grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(pct_legend)

pc_names <- colnames(pca_result_47$x)

var_explained_plot <- tibble(
  PC = factor(pc_names, levels = rev(pc_names)),
  variance_explained = as.numeric(var_explained)
  )

# Plot 2: Variance explained (convert to same % scale).
var_explained_plot$pct <- var_explained_plot$variance_explained * 100

p_var <- ggplot(var_explained_plot, aes(x = "", y = PC, fill = pct)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", width = 0.5,linewidth = 0.3 ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F0F0F0", high = "#B2182B", name = "%", limits = c(0, max_pct)) +
  labs(title = NULL, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), 
        legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.y =element_blank(),
        ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 16.5)
print(p_var)

### Save SVG files for import into Inkscape.
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir_plots, "p_pc.svg"),
  plot = p_pc,
  width = 1.9,
  height = 3,
  units = "in",
  device = svglite::svglite
)

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir_plots, "p_var.svg"),
  plot = p_var,
  width = 0.5,
  height = 2.9,
  units = "in",
  device = svglite::svglite
)

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir_plots, "pct_legend.svg"),
  plot = pct_legend,
  width = 1.25,
  height = 2.5,
  units = "in",
  device = svglite::svglite
)
```





### Generate marker-weight heatmaps grouped by strongest CV association.
### Figure 4B
```{r}
cv_colors <- list(
  CV = c(
    CV1 = "#E41A1C",
    CV2 = "#377EB8",
    CV3 = "#4DAF4A",
    CV4 = "#984EA3",
    CV5 = "#FF7F00",
    CV6 = "#A65628"
    )
)




### Make display copies so the original matrices remain unchanged.
coefs_U_plot <- coefs_U
coefs_V_plot <- coefs_V

rownames(coefs_V_plot) <- gsub("_c\\d+$","",rownames(coefs_V_plot))

### Create ordering and annotations after renaming.
tum_info <- order_markers_by_cv(coefs_U_plot)
imm_info <- order_markers_by_cv(coefs_V_plot)


cv_df <- data.frame(
  CV = factor(paste0("CV", 1:6), levels = paste0("CV", 1:6)),
  x = 1,
  y = 6:1
)

cv_fill <- c(
  CV1 = "#E41A1C",
  CV2 = "#377EB8",
  CV3 = "#4DAF4A",
  CV4 = "#984EA3",
  CV5 = "#FF7F00",
  CV6 = "#A65628"
)

p_cv_blocks <- ggplot(cv_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = CV)) +
  geom_tile(width = 0.95, height = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cv_fill) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = 6:1,
    labels = paste0("CV", 1:6),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 8,
      family = "sans",
      margin = margin(r = 3)
    ),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
  )



```





### Save heatmaps and legends
```{r}


shared_lim <- max(

### Exact same endpoint colours as the heatmaps.
weight_gradient <- linearGradient(
  colours = c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"),
  stops = c(0, 0.5, 1),
  x1 = unit(0.5, "npc"),
  y1 = unit(0, "npc"),

)

### Match PC legend bar size: 1.5 cm high x 0.3 cm wide.

  rectGrob(
    x = unit(0.42, "npc"),
    y = unit(0.5, "npc"),

  textGrob(
```
